title: Collision theory
examples: What makes a collision successful in a chemical reaction?
How does temperature affect the rate of a reaction?
Can you explain the role of activation energy in this theory?

explain.say: Today we are learning about collision theory. This theory explains how reactions happen. It suggests particles must collide with enough energy.
For a reaction to occur, particles must collide with the right energy. This minimum energy is called activation energy. The collision must overcome this energy barrier.
Not all collisions are successful. The particles also need to hit each other in the correct way. This correct way is called proper orientation.
Increasing the temperature increases the frequency of collisions. More energy means particles move faster and hit more often.
A real-life example is mixing baking soda and vinegar. They react quickly because the particles collide often and with enough energy.
A common mistake is thinking only high energy matters. You must remember that the collision must also have the right orientation.

faq.q: Does increasing temperature always speed up a reaction?
faq.a: Yes, generally increasing the temperature increases the kinetic energy of the particles. This leads to more frequent and more energetic collisions, speeding up the reaction rate. It is also called increasing the frequency of collisions.
asks: Why does heat speed up reactions?
What is the link between temperature and reaction speed?

faq.q: What is the difference between collision frequency and successful collision?
faq.a: Collision frequency is simply how often particles hit each other. A successful collision is a collision that has both enough energy and the correct orientation to cause a reaction. Not every collision works.
asks: How many collisions are needed for a reaction?

faq.q: Is the activation energy the same for all reactions?
faq.a: No, every different chemical reaction has its own unique activation energy. This value is specific to the reactants involved in that particular reaction. It is like a unique hurdle for that reaction.
asks: Does the reaction need a specific energy to start?
What is the energy barrier for this reaction?

faq.q: What does 'orientation' mean in this theory?
faq.a: Orientation refers to the specific way the reacting particles must be positioned when they collide. They must hit each other in a way that allows the bonds to break and reform correctly. It is about the angle of impact.
asks: Do the molecules need to line up?
What is the geometry of the collision?

faq.q: If I increase the pressure, does the rate increase?
faq.a: Increasing the pressure generally increases the concentration of the particles. Higher concentration means the particles are closer together, leading to a higher collision frequency and thus a faster rate. This is similar to increasing temperature.
asks: Does squeezing the gas speed up the reaction?
How does particle density affect the reaction rate?

facts: Collision theory states that reactions occur when particles collide.
A collision must have energy greater than the activation energy.
The particles must also have the correct relative orientation.
Increasing temperature increases the speed and frequency of collisions.

quiz.show: Rate increases due to more frequent collisions.
